COIN Stock Price Forecast: Morgan Stanley Cuts Price Target by Over 50% to $120, COIN Risks Falling to $100
sum: As of November 5 Eastern Time, Coinbase shares dropped 9.69% to $136.82 amid weak crypto trading activity. Morgan Stanley downgraded the stock to Underweight, slashing its price target from $258 to $120 while cutting long-term revenue and EBITDA forecasts. Q3 revenue fell 35% year-over-year to $1.22 billion, driven by lower transaction fees, though non-trading segments are expanding. Technically, the stock remains in a medium-term correction, trading below major moving averages with strong bearish momentum. Breaking below key support at $145 opens downside potential toward the $115 level, while overhead resistance clusters near the $145–$150 range.

TradingKey - As of the close on November 5 Eastern Time, Coinbase (COIN) shares fell 9.69% to close at $136.82, hitting an intraday low of $133.5, a new low since February 2024. Technical analysis shows that the stock's weekly chart continues to trade below major moving averages, and the medium-term correction structure has not significantly changed.

Morgan Stanley recently downgraded Coinbase to Underweight from Neutral and slashed its price target from $258 to $120, a cut of more than 53%. Analyst Michael Cyprys noted that subdued cryptocurrency trading activity recently, coupled with a weakening revenue outlook, has dampened confidence in the pace of Coinbase's earnings recovery.

Meanwhile, Morgan Stanley lowered its future earnings forecasts for Coinbase. Specifically, the 2027 revenue forecast was cut by 28% and the adjusted EBITDA forecast was lowered by 47%, while 2028 revenue and adjusted EBITDA forecasts were trimmed by 18% and 25%, respectively. The bank now expects Coinbase's 2028 normalized EBITDA to be approximately $2.4 billion, about 14% below 2025 levels, while lowering the valuation EBITDA multiple from 20x to 12x.

According to Coinbase's latest earnings report, the company generated approximately $1.22 billion in Q3 revenue, down 35% year over year. Within this, transaction revenue was around $590 million, down 44% year over year, while subscription and services revenue was around $570 million, down 20% year over year.

sum: Morgan Stanley downgraded Cisco Systems to Equal-weight from Overweight on Thursday, November 5, and cut its price target to 120 US dollars from 135 US dollars. The move came before Cisco's fiscal first-quarter results, with the bank arguing that the shares now offer a more balanced risk-reward profile.
Cisco Systems stock traded at 86.48 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 13:18 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026.

The downgrade was reported by Investing.com. Analyst Meta Marshall said Cisco's improving demand environment and artificial-intelligence opportunity still support the long-term investment case, but much of the rerating is already reflected in the shares.

Morgan Stanley said Cisco has gained 43 percent over the past 12 months, compared with a 14 percent rise for the S&P 500. The stock has consequently rerated to about 19 times forward earnings, bringing its valuation in line with the broader index.

The bank also pointed to two operating risks. Customers may have brought orders forward ahead of planned price increases, which could flatter near-term sales. At the same time, a larger share of lower-margin hardware sold to hyperscale customers could weigh on gross margins as Cisco expands its AI infrastructure business.

Marshall nevertheless expects Cisco to continue benefiting from earnings growth and sees several years of double-digit growth, particularly through cloud customers. Morgan Stanley said the growth mix will rely increasingly on AI revenue once the company moves beyond the effect of its pricing increases in fiscal 2028.

Cisco is scheduled to report its fiscal first-quarter results after the US market close on Thursday, November 12. Investors will focus on whether demand remains firm after pricing changes and whether the developing AI mix is putting pressure on profitability.

sum: Brokerages remained largely positive on State Bank of India (SBI) after the country's largest public sector lender reported a strong set of September quarter results for FY27. Strong net interest income (NII), improving margins and better asset quality supported the bank's performance, although slower-than-expected loan growth and higher operating expenses remained areas of concern.
JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, HSBC, Goldman Sachs and Citi retained their respective ratings on SBI, while several brokerages revised their target prices following the results.
SBI shares closed at Rs 970.25 on Tuesday, November 3, up 1.70 per cent, even as the stock market rallied close to 2 per cent.
SBI reported a 14 per cent year-on-year (YoY) increase in standalone net profit to Rs 23,038 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 20,160 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Net interest income increased 15 per cent YoY to Rs 49,143 crore. The growth was supported by an expansion in the bank's loan book, with gross advances crossing Rs 52 lakh crore during the quarter.

Operating profit rose 7 per cent to Rs 34,226 crore from Rs 31,904 crore a year earlier. Interest income increased 10 per cent to Rs 1.32 lakh crore, while interest expenses grew at a slower pace of 8 per cent to Rs 82,876 crore.
Lower provisions also supported profitability. Loan-loss provisions declined 33 per cent YoY to Rs 2,759 crore from Rs 4,132 crore.

Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley are dominating the AI stock boom. Here's their edge
sum: Fueled by the global boom in artificial intelligence stocks, relaxed capital rules and greater lending to hedge funds, big Wall Street banks have already had a banner year for equities trading — even with one quarter left to go.

The five biggest investment banks have generated about $67 billion in equities revenue through Sept. 30, according to company filings. That is $7 billion more than what the group made during all of 2025, which itself was a record haul.

But it's Wall Street's Big Three that have captured the largest slice of what is shaping up to be the industry's most lucrative arena: Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase and Morgan Stanley have made a combined $52 billion in stock trading revenue so far this year, nearly 80% of the total.

"When it comes to the AI mega trade, the Big Three consider each other their main competitors, and that's pretty much it," Mike Mayo, Wells Fargo banking analyst, told CNBC. "They've been best positioned to take advantage of this market."

Wall Street banks are experiencing an epic run of blockbuster profits as the total value of the stock market balloons and trading activity from institutional and retail investors rises across stocks, exchange-traded funds and derivatives. Helping drive this activity are the loans that the banks, through their prime brokerages, are extending to hedge funds so that they can amplify their bets.

Prime brokerage — the business of providing hedge funds with margin loans, securities lending and other trading services — has become a key battleground and source of growth. The Big Three's prime brokers are central to the larger equities story because they serve the largest funds across markets and products.
Demand for leverage to make bets on AI hardware, hyperscalers and chip suppliers has reached new heights, bank executives said last week.

sum: Stellantis (NYSE:STLA) shares fell more than 2% on Monday after Morgan Stanley downgraded the automaker to Underweight from Equal Weight and reduced its price target to $5.20 from $8.00.
The rating change formed part of a broader review of European automakers by analysts led by Javier Martinez de Olcoz Cerdan.

The analysts cited changes in Stellantis' inventories and incentives and said "the product pipeline is lagging behind peers," which they said could limit the company's ability to reduce investment as cash generation declines.
Morgan Stanley said Stellantis has "the widest risk/reward skew in the sector."
The analysts identified refinancing as one potential risk, while asset disposals or changes to the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement could affect the company's outlook in other scenarios.
Morgan Stanley separately upgraded Renault to Equal Weight from Underweight and increased its price target to €31 from €25.

The analysts described Renault as "the company with the largest increase in our estimates," citing its exposure to the European automotive market and the potential impact of regulatory measures concerning Chinese vehicle imports.

Morgan Stanley Gives Huge Stock Market Crash Warning in 30 Days
sum: Morgan Stanley told investors a stock market correction could arrive within 30 days. However, based on developments over the weekend, markets may not wait that long, with Monday likely to be the first test.
Mike Wilson, the bank's chief US equity strategist, is not worried about artificial intelligence (AI). He is worried about oil.
Wilson told Bloomberg that energy costs could starve the market of cash. US benchmark crude prices continue to hold above $100, up nearly 80% this year.
"I do think in the next 30 days, if oil goes to $120, $130, $140, that's a drain on liquidity," he said.
Wilson described market liquidity as sufficient for now, but not abundant.
He is not telling clients to sell. Instead, Morgan Stanley is rotating toward companies that generate cash internally, not cutting equity exposure.

Morgan Stanley began covering Coinbase (COIN) on September 10, its first call on the exchange since the 2021 listing. While the rating was equal weight, the price target is $250, representing a climb of almost 43% from the current price of $175.26.

Meta Stock Outlook: Named Top Pick by Morgan Stanley, Will the Stock Recover?
sum: Meta Platforms shares have declined significantly amid market concerns over the monetization of its heavy AI investments and ongoing losses from Reality Labs. Unlike cloud-based peers with direct enterprise revenue streams, Meta’s AI returns are reflected indirectly through advertising, pressuring short-term cash flow and profit margins. Despite soaring capital expenditures, Morgan Stanley named Meta a top pick, projecting 27% ad revenue growth in 2026. Technically, the stock remains in a downtrend below key moving averages, lacking reversal signals while hovering near support levels, though an oversold bounce remains possible if crucial thresholds are reclaimed.

TradingKey - Meta Platforms (META) shares have experienced a volatile decline since hitting a record high ($793) in August 2025. As of August 18 Eastern Time, based on a stock price of around $550, the drop during this period reached as much as roughly 30%.

By contrast, the Nasdaq 100 Index gained about 24% over the same period. Against the backdrop of the ongoing AI boom reshaping tech stock valuations, Meta bucked the trend with a notable decline, creating a stark divergence between its share price performance and the broader mega-cap tech sector. The main reason for this divergence is not that the market doubts Meta's AI capabilities, but rather that it questions the monetization ability of its AI business model.

Unlike Google (GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN), and Microsoft (MSFT), which can directly sell computing power to enterprise clients through cloud computing businesses, Meta's current AI investments primarily serve its own social platforms, advertising systems, AI assistants, and open-source models. The benefits brought by AI are mostly reflected in increased user engagement time, improved ad-matching efficiency, and potential new product opportunities, yet in the short term, it is difficult to break them out in financial reports as a clear, quantifiable revenue stream.

Whether Meta can gradually transform from a social media platform reliant on advertising monetization into a tech company boasting AI products, computing infrastructure, and diversified monetization channels will determine whether its stock price can reverse its weakness and regain market recognition.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Personally Joined a Closed-Door Morgan Stanley Roadshow to Address 3 Investor Concerns. Nvidia Stock Is Down 4% Since He Spoke.
sum: Jensen Huang, CEO of artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductor giant Nvidia (NVDA +4.04%), showed up at Morgan Stanley's Technology, Media & Telecom Conference in San Francisco in March with three important messages for investors.

This came at a time of growing anxiety among market participants about the potential returns -- or lack thereof -- from the $7 trillion expected to be spent globally on AI data centers by 2030. After soaring in recent years, Nvidia and other AI-related stocks have underperformed the broader market this year.
So it made sense that Huang, whose company is central to the AI revolution, would address some of these concerns that investors are beginning to feel.
Huang had three main messages for conference attendees, which included executives from almost 400 major global companies and over 2,000 capital allocators, according to the investment bank.
First, he said that rising demand for compute, the data processing that AI cloud centers deliver to users, translates directly into token generation, greater revenue, and higher GDP.

Tokens are the fundamental unit of AI work and consist of small chunks of output data; 100 tokens equal about 75 words of output. And the AI industry is beginning to view tokens as the primary measure of what it delivers, much like how electric utilities use kilowatt-hours to measure and bill for the electricity they provide.
Huang said that data centers are AI factories whose primary output is tokens, adding, "I'm certain compute equals revenues."

Morgan Stanley says buy these quality stocks. They also pay dividends
sum: As the market broadens out, investors should seek quality stocks, according to Morgan Stanley. On Tuesday , the Dow Jones Industrial Average rallied, while the Nasdaq Composite slipped. The Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK) reached its lowest level since May 7. Meanwhile, health care stocks and financials moved higher. The rotation toward quality now underway is a "classic mid-cycle transition as the business cycle matures," said Mike Wilson, Morgan Stanley's chief U.S. equity strategist. "From here, margin expansion is likely to depend less on early-cycle operating leverage and more on AI adoption, reinforcing our quality thesis," he wrote in a note Monday. "Near-term consolidation and even further downside toward 7000 remains possible if the war continues to escalate and/or the Fed unexpectedly hikes this week, but the quality rotation should ultimately support index resilience and even broad participation, albeit with different leadership." The S & P 500 is currently holding above 7,430. Wilson told CNBC's " Squawk Box " in an interview Tuesday that a 7,000 level on the broad market index "will be defended" and the benchmark should hit 8,000 by year end. In this environment, Morgan Stanley favors high free-cash-flow yield, low variability on earnings per share, strong balance sheets and high margins. Wilson and his team screened for those quality names that the firm rates overweight. Many of those stocks also pay income. Here are some of the dividend payers that made the cut. Coca-Cola , which has a 2.41% dividend yield, saw its shares jump more than 4% on Tuesday after its latest earnings report . The beverage giant beat on both the top and the bottom lines for the second quarter and also raised its full-year outlook. Last month, Morgan Stanley reiterated its overweight rating on the stock.

sum: An AI-powered trading and dealmaking binge boosted profits 58% at Morgan Stanley (MS) in the second quarter.

On Wednesday, the Wall Street bank reported net income of $5.58 billion, or $3.46 per share. Net revenue soared 27% from the year-ago period to $21.35 billion. Both earnings per share and revenue are record highs for Morgan Stanley.

Quarterly stock trading fees rose 69% from the year ago period to $6.3 billion, also the highest in the firm's history. Its equity underwriting businesses churned out $851 million, a 70% jump year over year and the highest since 2021.

The company exceeded analyst estimates for net income and revenue, capping off a banner week for Wall Street's biggest banks. JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Wells Fargo (WFC), Goldman Sachs (GS), Bank of America (BAC), and Citigroup (C) all reported earnings that surpassed expectations on Tuesday.
Together, these six big banks earned nearly $55 billion in the second quarter, a 37% jump a year earlier.
Morgan Stanley CEO Ted Pick called the results "exceptional" in a press release statement.
"We continue to accrete capital, giving us incremental flexibility to invest in our core businesses while generating strong returns for shareholders," Pick added.

sum: We recently published Jim Cramer's Biggest Winners to Buy: Top 20 AI & Other Stocks He Got Right in 2026. Morgan Stanley (NYSE:MS) is one of the stocks discussed by Jim Cramer.

Investment bank Morgan Stanley (NYSE:MS) is another stock that Jim Cramer has frequently discussed in 2026. The shares are up by 48% over the past year and by 17.6% year-to-date. Along with Cramer, several analysts have also discussed Morgan Stanley (NYSE:MS) this year. For instance, Bank of America raised the share price target to $225 from $220 and kept a Buy rating on the shares on April 16th. The bank remarked that it was optimistic that the remarks made by Morgan Stanley (NYSE:MS)'s during its latest earnings call would help with earnings and capital return growth. The investment bank's first quarter earnings saw it post $20.5 billion in net revenue and $5.6 billion in net income, which led its $3.43 in earnings per share to beat analyst estimates. Here is what Cramer said about Morgan Stanley (NYSE:MS) in January in his morning appearance:

"You know Ted is, Ted Pick is doing a great job. Remember my thesis, they've been taken down? Well because people just say, you know what, this group is not, these aren't semis, this is not AI, it's not semiconductors, in the end, it's finance and these stocks are up 35%. "Look I'm going to go against the market, I think the market's wrong on this, I think the market's trying to figure out, has it moved too much? And I think Ted Pick has reinvented this company, I got to salute him. . .but this Morgan Stanley model's a good one, David, it's very sticky, it's much less episodic, it deserves a much higher price-to-earnings multiple."
